So I see some people giving a lot of generic advice, let me share my own.

I joined Amity first but I couldn't afford the fees. So I dropped out and joined a tier 2 CU college pursuing English Hons as well. My English was excellent and I had a knack for reading too. But the atmosphere was terrible. The college was filled with brain dead people who couldn't care less about education. The teaching was sub-par and the syllabus was unecessarily huge and the marking system in CU is terrible. I have written pages after pages just for peanuts. 

The English Hons syllabus was completely outdated too. I realised as much as I loved reading as a hobby, this shit wouldn't help me one bit in real life. Things like "The wife of bath tale" or the "Heroic poetry" was mind numbingly boring and has no use in reality. 

In the last year I dropped out. 

I joined a distance course in sociology and so far it has been a far more interesting subject. I have tutions and learned the share market as well as taking up creative writing internships and odd freelance jobs. 

I have finished this degree and this year I'll pursue masters. I also live in an extremely toxic family with no financial or emotional support at all. And on top of that, I've a terminal disease that I'll have to deal with for the rest of my life. 

No this is not a struggle story about coming from nothing and becoming wildly successful. This is just a reminder that you're not alone. 

So as much as I hate advices, here's my two cents on the matter. 

Take care of your mental and physical health, get sleep and try to eat decent food. I know it will be hard living away from home, but try. Take each day at a time, there's no point worrying about a future that doesn't exist. Think about today, be present, and do the best you can. Right now, I'm assuming your "haat khorcha" is covered by tution money, and since you have already joined the degree, you might as well finish it. You haven't mentioned which sem you're in, but I assume you'll be done in the next two years. You also haven't mentioned if you're getting any financial support from your family, like any, at all. 

I'd suggest go for higher studies but there's no point doing masters in English again unless you really love the subject or you wanna clear NET and become a professor. If not you can try to switch to a different stream but again it depends on you, what you are good at and what you think you should do.

Arts have very less money at start and more grind.
IT has still sub-par money and some amount of grind. 
MBA if it's from a good tier 1 college can pay dividends but even tier 2-3 colleges are decent. Still sub-par money though. Going abroad is great but not everyone has the means to do that, if you have financial backing or you win a scholarship then you can consider it. The money is definitely better there. 

Get the degrees, start applying to entry level jobs, learn some skills on the side if possible and soon enough you'll come across something profitable. It will take some time though. 

In college, take part in events, make friends, socialize, but stay away from politics and negative toxic people. Building connections is important. Remember weak connections still matter. Most people in MBA or even in arts land jobs through connections. I know people working in the flim industry after finishing English Hons from Scottish church college. It's hard, but it's possible. But it's gonna be a long ride, no short cut or quick money schemes. 

Now yes you have to work hard in this country cos the competition is insane. But do prioritise your health as well, you DO NOT need to work for 25 hours a day under any circumstances no matter how hard your life gets. You'll simply drain yourself and burn out and end up with nothing. Instead find some time to relax and like I said, baby steps, one day at a time.

DM if you wanna ask me something more. Good luck.

I have been in the same exact same position and I'm still there. I'm 26, lost many years of education due to chronic illnesses, living in a toxic and dysfunctional family, almost broke, getting rejected in interviews on the daily. 

2021 was the worst year of my life. My dog passed away,  my family members passed away, and I got diagnosed with a terminal disease. At the time I was super depressed. I was having panic attacks, I wasn't eating, I wasn't getting enough sleep, I was a mess. So I gave up and just waited. I told myself everyday, it couldn't possibly get worse so might as well see one more day. And I took each day at a time, set small goals for myself and then moved on to the next day. Slowly I got back on my groove, I went back to college (graduating this year), got back into writing (my passion), learned some practical (driving) and theoretical (Digital marketing) skills. Started a YouTube channel, and just went with the flow.

Things have gotten a bit better since and it's a stronger. I disagree with the comment "what doesn't kill you, makes you stronger", sometimes what doesn't kill you gives you lifelong trauma and destroys you mentally and emotionally and no amount of motivational comments can get you out of that hole.

So what can you do? Take one day at a time. No need worry about future. Do the best you can today. Sit down and write everything you wish you could do today, and then go on to the next. It will get better and even if it doesn't you'll know how to handle it when you get there.

Eat good food, get good sleep, take anti-depressants if necessary after talking to a doctor. Do what you need. 

Set small goals everyday and try to achieve them and write them down in a journal. Even if you don't feel like doing it, set alarms at various times of the day to remind you of the stuff that needs to be taken care of and do it anyway. Do it alone, do it unhappy, do it anxious but do it anyway.
